 Live Updates: Election Day: Israelis flock to polls as turnout surges to 31.5% nationwide, highest since 1973
 'They're trying to steal the election': Netanyahu warns of high Arab voter turnout • Politicians continue reporting fraud attempts, missing ballots at polling stations across Israel
 Follow us on Google ㅤ October 27, 1:14 PM 
 Parties sidestep app ban inside polling stations, asking voters outside to identify themselves
 Barred from using voter-tracking apps inside polling stations, parties including Likud and United Torah Judaism stationed activists outside to ask voters to identify themselves and log their turnout.

 By JERUSALEM POST STAFF October 27, 11:53 AM 
 Hendel's Reservists Party files complaint over missing, defaced ballot slips
 By SHIR PERETS The Reservists party chairman Yoaz Hendel speaks during an election conference at Tel Aviv University, ahead of Israel’s upcoming general elections, October 18, 2026. ( photo credit : AVSHALOM SASSONI/FLASH90 ) Load More Israel votes 2026: All you need to know 
 Some 7.3 million eligible Israelis will decide between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing bloc and Gadi Eisenkot's diverse opposition bloc.
 A party must receive at least 3.25% of valid votes to enter the Knesset.
 Most polling stations are open from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. Some locations have different hours.
 The Jerusalem Post will provide real-time election coverage throughout the day, including a live broadcast of the exit polls and their implications, starting from 9:30 p.m.
